diagnostic_evidence.quote: Graph-tree-induced edge coefficients are invariant to the choice of terminals up to a common factor.
where $y_\tau$ is the restriction of the vector of $(G,\tau)$-induced coefficients to the set of $\tau$'s edges
Let us denote $e_0$'s vertices by $l$ and $r$ and treat them as the terminals.
the positive sign corresponds to $e$ oriented from $l$ to $r$

issues.failure_explanation: The vector y_tau is defined relative to one fixed terminal pair, and the sign convention 'oriented from l to r' depends on that pair. The proof of the eigen-equation Y_tau y_tau = (1/n) y_tau is carried out one row at a time. For each row e_0 the terminals are re-chosen as the endpoints of e_0, and all edges are re-oriented from l to r. The rows therefore use possibly different vectors, with different st-orientations and different psi-values. They combine into a statement about a single vector only if the coefficients for different terminal pairs are proportional, including the signs. That is exactly Proposition prop:added-1, whose proof is omitted. It is not a routine remark. Unlike for the weights, the transformation depends on tau through psi. One must show that passing to the complement of a subgraph maps psi to -psi, and one must track the orientation signs. Without this, only one row of the eigen-equation is checked for each of several different vectors, and the claim that 1/n is an eigenvalue of every tree submatrix is not established.

failure_location.quote: We leave it as an exercise for the reader to prove the following property.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove prop:added-1 in the style of the proof of the weight-invariance proposition. Re-rooting the decomposition tree at an edge replaces each subgraph by its complement in G with the same terminals. Exactly one of a subgraph and its complement contains the tau-path between the terminals, so psi(complement) = -psi(Gamma). The ratios in the product formula are then preserved up to a common factor, with orientation signs tracked. Conclude that the vectors for different terminal pairs are proportional with a nonzero factor.
issues.overall_effect: The eigenvalue 1/n of every spanning-tree submatrix is not rigorously established. The lower bound arccos(1/sqrt(n)) in the main theorem, and the sharpness corollary that rests on it, are therefore not fully proved.
issues.title: Terminal-invariance of the (G,tau)-induced coefficients is left unproved but is essential to the proof of the main theorem
issues.why_classification: The result is very likely true, and a contained lemma analogous to the existing weight-invariance proof closes the gap without changing the method, statement or rate. It is still a genuine lemma with sign bookkeeping, not an omitted line of algebra, so it is more than minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the star spaces of all nontrivial 2-connected series-parallel graphs on $k + 1$ vertices and $n$ edges
the search ended with a single match found
Number of symmetry classes of extremal subspaces for various $n$ and $k$.

issues.failure_explanation: For k=2 the relevant graphs are 2-connected multigraphs on 3 vertices, namely triangles with edge multiplicities (a,b,c), each at least 1, summing to n. The associated matroid depends only on the multiset {a,b,c}, so the number of classes is the number of partitions of n into exactly three parts. For n=3,...,9 this gives 1,1,2,3,4,5,7. For n=9 the seven classes are (7,1,1), (6,2,1), (5,3,1), (5,2,2), (4,4,1), (4,3,2), (3,3,3). The table lists 6 for n=9, k=2 and, by the duality symmetry, 6 for k=7. This contradicts the paper's own description of the extremal subspaces. It also contradicts the asserted exact match of the whole triangle with the series-parallel-matroid counts.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the two entries to 7 after checking the n=9 row. If the experiments really found only 6 classes, state that the search for n=9 was incomplete instead of claiming an exact match.
issues.overall_effect: The empirical table, and the claim that it exactly reproduces the series-parallel matroid triangle, are wrong in two symmetric entries of the last row. No formal theorem depends on it.
issues.title: Table entry for n=9, k=2 (and symmetric k=7) contradicts the paper's own characterization and claimed OEIS match
issues.why_classification: Only two numerical entries of an empirical motivating table are wrong. They are fixed by a local correction or a one-sentence caveat, and no proved result or main claim is affected.
